content.jointProblem: How can Latin–Cyrillic script normalisation and/or script-unified retrieval be integrated into Lex Automatika's PostgreSQL full-text search pipeline so that mixed-script Serbian contracts are found regardless of the query script, without materially increasing search latency? The collaboration would test indexing-time, query-time and hybrid transliteration strategies on the company's contract corpus and search logs.

rationale.text: Petrović has direct evidence on Serbian retrieval with mixed Latin/Cyrillic corpora and on script normalisation as a preprocessing step that improves retrieval quality.

sources.quote: the corpus contains both Latin and Cyrillic script
We further study the effect of script normalisation as a preprocessing step and show that it consistently improves retrieval quality.

rationale.text: He has proposed a script-unified embedding approach that maps Latin-script and Cyrillic-script Serbian sentences into a shared vector space.

sources.quote: This paper proposes a script-unified embedding approach that maps Latin-script and Cyrillic-script Serbian sentences to a shared vector space.

rationale.text: His Serbian pretraining work explicitly addresses mixed-script documents in the data pipeline.

sources.quote: including mixed-script documents, informal spelling variations, and code-switched passages

rationale.text: His SRB-NLP project is centrally concerned with supporting both Latin and Cyrillic scripts on equal footing.

sources.quote: A central objective is ensuring that all resources support both Latin and Cyrillic scripts on equal footing.

constraints.text: The solution must be integrated with or around the existing PostgreSQL full-text search pipeline, because the company has diagnosed script separation in the PostgreSQL FTS index.

sources.quote: The root cause is that our full-text search index in PostgreSQL treats the two scripts as completely different character sets.

constraints.text: The approach must support mixed-script documents, not only documents written fully in one script.

sources.quote: We want a solution that is robust enough to handle mixed-script documents, not just fully-Cyrillic or fully-Latin ones

constraints.text: The transliteration logic must address dialect-dependent ambiguities where one Latin sequence can map to different Cyrillic letters.

sources.quote: there are edge cases where the same Latin sequence maps to different Cyrillic letters depending on dialect conventions.

constraints.text: Search response times must not noticeably degrade after the change.

sources.quote: does not slow down search response times noticeably

constraints.text: Company engineering time for the work is limited to one backend engineer for up to six weeks, so the scope must fit a short pilot or be supplemented by other resources.

sources.quote: We have one backend engineer who can work on this for up to six weeks.

constraints.text: Evaluation should use or reproduce the January 2024 search-log sample so that the roughly one-in-five zero-hit problem can be measured before and after the change.

sources.quote: We estimated this affects roughly one in five searches based on a sample we pulled from server logs in January 2024.

risks: The researcher's retrieval evidence is on customer-support question answering and related Serbian benchmarks, not on legal contract search or PostgreSQL full-text search; transfer to KlozuraPro's contract index is unproven and should be the first experiment.

The cross-script training approach uses automatically generated parallel pairs obtained by deterministic transliteration, so it may not cover the company's dialect-dependent Latin-to-Cyrillic ambiguities without additional mapping rules.
The company has only one backend engineer for up to six weeks, which may be insufficient for production integration, evaluation and latency testing; a pilot scope should be agreed before starting.
Milan Petrović's availability is unknown from the participation data, so his capacity for a joint project must be confirmed.

Client contracts are sensitive documents; the company's information-security policy is self-assessed against ISO 27001, so data-access and anonymisation arrangements must be agreed before tests on real contracts.
questions: Can Milan Petrović confirm his availability and capacity for a joint project, and would the company or researcher also consider an industrial PhD supervision format?
Should transliteration be placed at indexing time, query time, or both, and can the project access the PostgreSQL FTS configuration plus the January 2024 search-log sample?
What latency budget and zero-hit-rate target would count as success, and which mixed-script contract documents can be used for evaluation?
Which dialect conventions or transliteration table should be authoritative for Serbian legal contracts with ambiguous Latin-to-Cyrillic mappings?
What data-access, anonymisation and confidentiality constraints apply to client contracts during testing?
Can the company's two ML engineers support the one backend engineer beyond the six-week window if the pilot shows promise?
